rights.principle:
The website_licensing section records the explicit default license for
eligible public sragi.org content. It does not license the wider ecosystem.
Rights are determined by the license identifier, license expression,
rights statement, contract and applicable law governing each artifact.
rights.unspecified_artifact_policy:
On sragi.org, eligible public content without a different license notice
is covered by the express website policy. Outside that defined scope,
no license grant should be inferred.
rights.third_party_policy:
Third-party material remains governed by its applicable third-party
license, rights statement or agreement. First-party metadata cannot
expand, replace or override third-party rights.
rights.non_override_rule:
No statement in this framework expands, reduces or replaces rights
explicitly granted or reserved at artifact level.

licensing.rule:
Every SRAGI artifact SHOULD identify its applicable license, license
expression, rights statement or governing terms. Where attached, that
information is authoritative. Eligible public sragi.org content may inherit
the explicit website default; products and other artifacts retain their
applicable terms. No ecosystem-wide default overrides artifact rights.
licensing.future_compatibility:
New artifact classes, technologies, media, AI systems, distribution
mechanisms, business models and licensing approaches may be added
without replacing the core artifact-level rights architecture.

website_licensing.title: SRAGI.org website licensing policy
website_licensing.grant:
Unless otherwise indicated, eligible public content on sragi.org that
Neptunia Media AS owns or is authorized to license follows the configured
website default license identified by this policy.
website_licensing.exceptions:
Third-party rights are an overriding boundary and remain governed by their
own terms. For Neptunia-controlled material, a license notice, SPDX expression,
rights statement or applicable agreement attached to a specific artifact
takes precedence over the website default. Separately licensed products,
frameworks, software, downloads and embedded components retain their stated
terms. The website default does not grant trademark rights.
website_licensing.machine_use:
Search engines, AI systems and other machine agents are welcome to access
public content. No crawler fee, registration or license token is required
by this website access policy. AI use, including training, follows the
governing website or artifact license and applicable law. Artifact-specific
terms continue to govern exceptions; this policy does not waive their
obligations or turn commercial products into free grants.
website_licensing.scope_rule:
This is an explicit website policy, not a license for every SRAGI artifact
or repository. Public availability alone does not establish ownership or
sufficient third-party rights. Existing grants are not revoked.

open_knowledge.description: Knowledge, theory, articles, research and documentation.

open_frameworks.description: SRAGI instruction frameworks, YAML resources and skills.

software.description: Executable software, source code, libraries and integrations.

selection_guidance.Apache-2.0: Preferred where patent licensing or enterprise implementation considerations are material.
selection_guidance.CC0-1.0: Preferred where maximum unrestricted reuse is the primary objective.

commercial.name: SRAGI® Commercial Suite License
commercial.description:
Alternative commercial licensing terms available from Neptunia Media AS.
For eligible CC BY-SA artifacts, the primary commercial function is an
agreed exception from the ShareAlike obligation within the licensed scope,
together with any additional rights expressly activated by agreement.
The presence of this LicenseRef does not itself grant commercial rights.

future.description: Additional license classes may be introduced without changing the core architecture.

dual_licensing.interpretation:
OR denotes alternative licensing paths subject to the terms applicable to
the selected path. Commercial activity alone does not require the SRAGI
Commercial Suite. For eligible artifacts on the CC BY-SA path, the commercial
path may provide an agreed exception from ShareAlike within the licensed scope,
plus other expressly activated rights or terms.

commercial.grant_rule:
Commercial-license rights arise only through an applicable commercial
agreement with Neptunia Media AS and only within its licensed scope.

sharealike_exception.rule:
Where an eligible artifact is offered under CC-BY-SA-4.0 OR
LicenseRef-SRAGI-Commercial, an applicable commercial agreement may permit
the licensee to use, modify and distribute the licensed material within
the agreed scope without the ShareAlike obligation that would otherwise
apply under the CC BY-SA 4.0 path.
sharealike_exception.limits:
The exception applies only to the Licensed Materials and scope expressly
identified in the commercial agreement. It does not remove attribution,
third-party, trademark, certification, partner or other obligations unless
those rights are separately and expressly granted.

profiles.principle:
Professional, Organization, Enterprise, Developer, OEM/Embedded, Vertical
and Sovereign are scope, pricing and rights profiles under one commercial
licensing architecture; they are not separate master licenses.

rsl.rule:
RSL references the explicit website policy for the site-wide scope,
including its configured default and artifact/third-party exceptions.
Verified artifact records may reference their standard license directly.
No crawler fee or license token is introduced. SPDX identifies licenses;
RSL 1.0 and SRLF 2.0 remain independently versioned.

machine_access.access_policy:
Public SRAGI resources should by default be technically accessible for
discovery, crawling, indexing and retrieval by search engines, AI systems,
research crawlers and other machine agents.

agents.rule: Named agents are explicitly welcomed as policy signals; the robots mechanism uses the wildcard so unlisted agents remain equally welcome.

machine_access.rights_rule:
Technical access, crawler accessibility, indexing or discovery metadata
does not independently grant copyright or other intellectual-property rights.
Rights relating to an artifact are determined by its applicable license,
rights statement, contract and law, including the explicit website default
where its scope applies.

ai_training.rule:
Rights relating to AI training are determined by the governing license,
rights statement, contract and law, including the express website default
for eligible public content without a different notice.

interpretation.ai_training_and_adaptation:
This framework does not determine whether AI training, model development,
model outputs or related machine-learning activities constitute Adapted
Material or trigger particular obligations under an applicable license.
Such questions are governed by the applicable license,
applicable law and the circumstances of the specific use.

attribution.rule: Attribution requirements are determined by the applicable artifact license.

preferred_machine_attribution.note: This does not replace or reduce requirements imposed by the artifact license.

open_license_layer.invitation:
SRAGI invites people, organizations and AI systems to use knowledge in
ways that increase life, learning, resilience, reciprocity and regenerative
capacity. Unless incorporated into a separate binding agreement, these
principles are aspirational and add no restriction to an open license.

commercial_covenant.rule:
A commercial agreement may expressly define measurable regenerative
commitments appropriate to the licensed use, organization or deployment.

contributions.principle:
SRAGI may accept third-party contributions only under terms compatible with
the licensing model applicable to the resulting artifact.
contributions.sufficient_rights_definition:
For an artifact offered under both an open path and
LicenseRef-SRAGI-Commercial, sufficient rights means a documented grant,
assignment or agreement broad enough for Neptunia Media AS to distribute
the contribution under the applicable open license and to sublicense or
relicense it under the applicable commercial terms. A DCO alone documents
provenance and authority to contribute; it does not by itself grant
commercial relicensing rights.

commercial_relicensing.rule:
A contribution may be included in an artifact offered under
LicenseRef-SRAGI-Commercial only where Neptunia Media AS possesses
sufficient rights to license that contribution under the commercial terms.

contributions.employer_and_client_rights:
Contributors must ensure that employer, client or other third-party rights
do not prevent the intended contribution or licensing model. Where required,
authority or permission must be documented before merge.
contributions.fallback:
Contributions lacking sufficient commercial licensing rights must not be
represented as available under LicenseRef-SRAGI-Commercial.

contributor_rights.principle:
Contributor terms should obtain only the rights necessary for
the applicable SRAGI licensing and distribution model while
preserving clear provenance and authorship records.

trademark.principle:
Copyright, content and software licenses do not automatically grant trademark,
certification, partnership, endorsement or branding rights.

levels.powered_by_SRAGI:
Limited permission to state that SRAGI® is an important technology or
framework component in the licensed product or service.
levels.guided_by_SRAGI:
Limited permission to state that SRAGI® materially guides the methodology
or operating approach of the licensed product, service or organization.
levels.governed_by_SRAGI:
Limited permission to state that SRAGI® is used as an agreed governance
or operating framework. This is not certification.

third_party.rule:
Neptunia Media AS can grant only rights it owns, controls or is otherwise
authorized to license. Third-party materials remain governed by their terms.

publication.generation_principle:
Generated representations may contain relevant subsets of this framework.
They must preserve the distinction between technical access, rights discovery
and legal license grants and must not alter artifact-specific rights.

repository_file_policy.rule:
This list is a map of canonical and generated resources, not a closed schema.
File presence or omission does not determine artifact rights.

evolution.rule:
Framework changes are versioned. Existing artifacts remain governed by the
terms applicable to their released version unless an authorized rights holder
expressly relicenses them. New framework versions do not retroactively change
previously granted rights.

history.summary:
Artifact-level rights authority; scoped CC BY website policy; SPDX/RSL
discovery; commercial ShareAlike-exception path; contributor-rights
integrity; trademark separation; provenance and long-horizon extensibility.
Previous layered model using CC BY 4.0 as ecosystem default.
